pr_body:
All major Android devices have issues opening more "fine grain" audio channel configurations besides Stereo, 5.1 or .7.1 - use AE's feature to silently add additional channels so that e.g. 3.0, 4.0, 4.1, etc. are tunneled via 5.1, 7.1 and rest is sent via stereo.

The issue is here not kodi, but Android not being able to open the mask, throwing channels away while accepting the input without error.

Fixes:  #24546
pr_comments: So - whatever comes up as regressions I will take up directly, which is why I did not wait longer with merging.

issue_context.title: Kodi Omega Android Nightly - Quad plays as 'Dolby Audio' (stereo only)
issue_context.body:
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
Here is a clear and concise description of what the problem is:
I have recently started testing various surround/spatial audio formats on a new Amazon Firestick 4K Max (2nd gen 2023) using latest Kodi v21 Omega Android nightlies.

When I play  Quad FLAC music file with less than 6 channels my AVR shows it is receiving Stereo only (the Denon AVR shows 'Dolby Audio') which then is upmixed by the AVR - wrong).

This is a critical bug for users with Quad music collections.


## Expected Behavior
Here is a clear and concise description of what was expected to happen:
All Quad formatted files should play as multi-channel files (not stereo) with the discreet channels sent to the AVR, just like they always have in previous Kodi releases (and do now with LibreElec v21 nightly)


## Actual Behavior
Quad in a 5.1 formatted file (Quad + Silent C and Silent LFE) - this plays a quad on the FTV (correct)
Quad in a 5.0 formatted file (Quad + Silent C) - stereo output only (wrong)
Quad in a 4.0 formatted file (Quad with channel mask L, R, Ls, Rs) - stereo output only (wrong)
Quad in a 4.0 formatted file (Quad with channel mask L, R, Lb Rb - stereo output only (wrong)


## Possible Fix
These exact same files ALL play correctly in LibreElec v12 Beta 2 Generic (Kodi v21 Omega build 17 Jan). These same files have always played correctly in recent Kodi releases (Matrix etc). I assume the Kodi IEC Packer needs a fix (unsure).


### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
I have created 4 x 30 sec FLAC test files with the typical channel layouts used by Quad enthusiasts over the years:

Link to zip file containing 4 x FLACs and a FTV Kodi.log file: (78MB)
https://1drv.ms/u/s!Aqs3ia6BNDDHsAwowhnjZHCusXcy?e=zTJXy7

Play these on a Fire TV 4K Max with Kodi Omega Nightly (I suspect other Android devices may have same issue)

### Debuglog
The debuglog can be found here:
A Kodi.log file is in the test file zip linked above:

### Screenshots 
Here are some links or screenshots to help explain the problem:
(none)

## Additional context or screenshots (if appropriate)
Here is some additional context or explanation that might help:
Historically  Quad enthusiasts have decoded 4 channel FLAC. Mnay AVR could not play pur 4 channel files so the 4 different formats in the test files are all very commonly used. Kodi needs to support all 4 to be used in the quad community. (it always has BTW)

Team Kodi will consider your problem report however, we will not make any promises the problem will be solved.*

We are succesfully opening exactly the same 4 channels we open on windows. The rest is done - as always - and you should know that from the forum by the FireTV firmware.

You can influence that amazon firmware a bit by setting Sound to "PCM" in their settings, that should make the 4.0 work, but is most likely not what you like. Additionally some people report success when setting their AVR to "PURE DIRECT".

In general I have to tell everyyone who reads this:

Kodi does on Android THE 100% EXACT thing as it does on WASAPI or on ALSA. It opens AudioTrack with the best available format - but after that Android is free to do whatever it wants without a single influence by kodi.

That looks like this:

2.0 PCM -> SampleRate of Input / Float32
Multi-Channel-PCM -> SampleRate of Input / S16NE, cause Android devices (besides the Shield) can only output multi channel in 16 bit precision.

PS: File that bug with amazon.

There was wise kodi developer some years ago: "First decide for the features you need, then decide for your hardware!"

@thexai if you have a minute could you test one of those 4.0 samples and see if the Shield also does not properly handle it? If no device can ... we simply play it as 5.1 with the additional channels muted.

---------
2.0 PCM -> SampleRate of Input / Float32
Multi-Channel-PCM -> SampleRate of Input / S16NE, cause Android devices (besides the Shield) can only output multi channel in 16 bit precision.
-----------

The Fire TV 4K Max 2nd gen (2023) spec state:
PCM/Wave. Up to 192 kHz, 8 channels, 16-bit and **24-bit**

I'm wondering whether its possible to to test 24 bit since Kodi is forcing S16NE (16 bit conversion)

"Since kodi is forcing". I always like that ... as you cannot approach closed development team of amazon and simply ask what they do in firmware  ... kodi, the oss evil in the game ... 

Android is not so flexible as you think it is. Also kodi is not a shield mediaplayer or a amazon mediaplayer. 

Why not play your 4.0 audio files with exoplayer? What do you get? 24 bit precission and 4.0 channels?

Read: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/AudioFormat#encoding
Test: https://jenkins.kodi.tv/job/android-arm-docker/5285/artifact/kodi-20240120-4977d536-hdr-armeabi-v7a.apk

This outputs highest quality from kodi as to the Android specification Float32. Reason: all ffmpeg decoders decode into float .

What you also might not have gotten: Kodi uses Audiotrack, we don't program / write to the hardware,  but talk to this sound server - it can decide whatever it wants as you see with your quad 4.0.

Therefore with above build, kodi outputs the absolute highest quality Android can cope with - and even better: the audiotrack can decide if it outputs it as 24 bit or 32 bit (both exist on Android) or even fallback to 16bit.

Curious if you see a difference in the "sample format" your AVR receives. Channel stuff stays the same or if it works at all ;-)

PS: I read amazon's exoplayer source, it's on github. They either output float32 or int16 ... so then - what above linked build does, is what you can expect on amazon hw / sw.

I think also this time their 24 bit and HighPrecision is only meant for Stereo Output. You will tell us.

@fritsch I had already found the Android AudioFormat info and was starting to read about compiling Android Kodi to do my own testing on using a 32bit AudioFormat (I assumed this was a dead issue as far as you were concerned). Thank you for continuing to look at this.

GOOD NEWS: Using your latest Jenkins build
96kHz FLAC is output at 96kHz to my AVR!!
The two of test Quads are outputting 4 channel audio (in 5.1 format) and playing correctly!! **
192kHz multichannel is playing correctly (192kHz showing on my AVR)

This is awesome! THANK YOU!!!

What can be done to get any of your changes into the official Kodi Android build?

If it cant be added I'll fork and maintain/build with these fixes moving forward for the users over on QuadraphonicQuad forum. (and anyone else into highres audio on the FTV)

https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/AudioFormat#CHANNEL_OUT_QUAD <- constant value: 204 -> now, check your original logfile:
2024-01-20 15:13:42.599 T:7237     info <general>: Trying to open: samplerate: 96000, **channelMask: 204,** encoding: 2

See, this is what I tried to tell you before. We _exactly_ and 100% opened CHANNEL_OUT_QUAD and this is exactly what your device ignores and does not understand. The speaker masks in Android work like this: FL | FR | BL | BR = 0x08 | 0x04 | 0x80 | 0x40 == 0xee == 204 == CHANNEL_OUT_QUAD

So - yeah, kodi is programmed to end up 100% with the perfect channel mask, which your device does not support, which is why it needed filling up.

b) Exactly. And I kindly asked you to check what your AVR **receives**. If you find one yourself let him play your 4 samples, provide debuglog (while it will look exactly like yours) and say what output he / she got.
